response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-19
CLINICAL INDICATION: On treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer. Increasing shortness of breath over one week.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. M. Castellanos (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-09-02
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same projection. The prior is displayed with higher contrast than the current, and the prior appears mildly rotated while the current is straight. Both differences limit comparison of subtle hilar density and hilar size.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None. No time-sensitive findings flagged.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is central with the expected slight rightward deviation at the aortic arch. No central airway narrowing at this resolution. Lung volumes are large. No focal consolidation, collapse or discrete mass in any zone. Mildly coarse markings in the right lower zone, without focal consolidation, similar to the prior (one read only; overlying soft tissue may contribute). Mildly prominent bronchovascular markings at the right base, similar on both studies (one read only; some haze may be overlying breast soft tissue). Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. A tiny density over the right medial upper zone near the anterior first rib end is seen on the prior only (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle is prominent, consistent with an unfolded aorta, and similar to the prior. Upper mediastinum is not widened. Right hilum is unremarkable. Left hilum: INDETERMINATE. The reads did not agree on whether it has changed. One read found the left hilum fuller and denser on the prior and less conspicuous on the current, which suggests it may be smaller, but the difference could be explained by the prior's higher contrast and mild rotation. The other read found the left hilum fuller and denser than the right on both studies with similar contour and bulk. The current left hilum is not bulky. A small ring lucency projects over it on the current study, possibly a bronchus seen end-on (see CAN'T DETERMINE). Measurement is needed and none is available.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles are sharp on both studies. No pleural line and no visible pleural thickening. Diaphragm: the left dome is level with or slightly higher than the right on both studies, the reverse of the usual relationship. Gas-filled stomach and bowel lie under the left dome and partly overlap the left base. No gas under the right dome. Change in gas distension under the left dome is INDETERMINATE: the reads disagreed, one calling it stable and the other calling it decreased on the current.
- Heart: Not enlarged on this PA film. Cardiac silhouette is at the upper limit of normal with sharp borders, and size and contour are similar to the prior (one read only).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion at this resolution. Degenerative change at both shoulders and in the lower cervical spine. No soft tissue gas. Fine bone detail is limited on both images. Devices: a left-sided central venous catheter enters from the left lateral chest or axillary region and crosses the midline, with its tip projecting over the right paramediastinal region at the expected level of the superior vena cava. Course and tip position match the prior. No new device. The insertion site is not on the film.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: No change confirmed. Indeterminate: left hilar size and density (reads did not agree; prior appears fuller and denser, possibly due to contrast and rotation). Indeterminate: gas distension under the left dome (reads disagreed; less on the current per one read). Tiny right medial upper zone density seen on the prior only (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle and mediastinal width. Left central venous catheter course and tip position. Coarse right lower zone markings. Heart size and contour (similar). Sharp costophrenic angles. High left dome relationship. No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax or new nodule or mass.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the left hilum truly smaller on the current study than on the prior? | Reason: The prior has higher contrast and mild rotation, and both can make one hilum look larger and denser. A frontal film alone does not separate vessel from node or mass. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast, and review of the source images in PACS.
- Is the tiny density over the right medial upper zone on the prior a lung nodule or first rib costochondral calcification? | Reason: The density is well under the size at which X-ray separates a nodule from bone or a vessel end-on. It is not clearly seen on the lower-contrast current film. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. CT chest if it persists on review.
- Is there opacity behind the heart or at the left base? | Reason: The relatively high left dome and gas-filled bowel overlap the left base and retrocardiac region on a frontal film alone. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest.
- Is there a focal bone lesion in the ribs, shoulders or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS.
- Is the left hilar fullness vascular (pulmonary artery) or nodal? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessel from lymph node, and the difference in image contrast between the two studies limits judgment of subtle density change. | Recommend: Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging. If none is available, contrast-enhanced CT chest.
- Is the small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study a bronchus seen end-on or a small cavitary or cystic focus? | Reason: The structure is small, overlaps hilar vessels, and is seen on a downsampled frontal image only. It is less conspicuous on the higher-contrast prior. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. Lateral view or CT chest if it persists.
- Does the asymmetry of the breast shadows reflect previous left breast surgery, or positioning? | Reason: Soft-tissue contours are partly outside the field and faint at this resolution. The asymmetry makes the right lower zone look hazier than the left on both studies. | Recommend: Correlate with surgical history. Do not read the right lower zone haze as lung opacity without that correlation.
- What is the exact catheter tip position relative to the cavoatrial junction, and what type of line is it? | Reason: The carina and the right atrial junction are not sharply defined on these images, and the insertion site and any reservoir lie outside the field. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Correlate with the line insertion record.
- Are there small nodules in the retrocardiac region, at the apices or behind the diaphragm domes? | Reason: Only a single frontal view of each study is available. These areas are hidden by overlap, and small nodules cannot be separated from vessels seen end-on or from rib ends. | Recommend: Lateral view, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, and fine bone detail such as cortex, pedicles and small lucent lesions is not reliably shown. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.

IMPRESSION:
1. Left hilum: change is indeterminate. The prior shows a fuller, denser left hilar shadow than the current, and the reads did not agree on whether this is a true change. Differences in image contrast and rotation may account for it. No measurement is available, and vessel versus node cannot be separated on a frontal film. Contrast-enhanced CT chest is recommended.
2. Small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study, possibly a bronchus seen end-on. A small cavitary or cystic focus is not excluded on this film. Left hilar contour is otherwise similar on both studies by one read.
3. Mildly coarse right lower zone markings, without focal consolidation, similar to the prior (one read only). Overlying soft tissue may contribute.
4. Mildly prominent bronchovascular markings at the right base, similar to the prior (one read only). Some haze may be overlying breast soft tissue.
5. Heart not enlarged, at the upper limit of normal, with similar size to the prior (one read only).
6. No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new nodule or mass is seen compared with the prior. This single frontal film does not show a cause for the breathlessness, and the unresolved left hilar question remains. Triage: high urgency, not paged; radiologist review needed.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the left hilar question and the other items listed above. Interval is not specified in the findings; timing to be set by the radiologist.
- Lateral chest view or CT chest for the left base, retrocardiac region and possible small nodules.
- Review source images in PACS for the right upper zone density on the prior, the left hilar ring lucency, bone detail and catheter tip position.
- Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging, surgical history and the line insertion record.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
